;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[2019 Loralai attack]]
**Nine people, including civilians and [[Law enforcement in Pakistan|policemen]], are dead and 22 others are injured after gunmen and suicide bombers attacked a [[Deputy inspector general of police|Deputy Inspector General]] (DIG) office in Pakistan's [[Loralai]]. The [[Tehrik-i-Taliban]] claim responsibility for the attack. [https://tribune.com.pk/story/1899305/1-least-five-injured-loralai-terrorist-attack/ (''Express Tribune'')]
*[[Somali Civil War]]
**Two people were killed and five others were injured in a car bombing near the Somali Petroleum Ministry and the responsibility was claimed by Al-Shabaab. [https://www.nation.co.ke/news/africa/Two-killed-in-Mogadishu-car-bombing/1066-4956772-f9lt47z/index.html (''Daily Nation'')]
*A double bombing injures three police officers in [[Tehran]], [[Iran]]. [https://www.seattletimes.com/nation-world/nation/double-bombing-wounds-3-police-in-iran/ (''The Seattle Times'')]
;Business and economics
*[[2017 California wildfires]], [[2018 California wildfires]]
**[[Pacific Gas and Electric Company]] files for [[Chapter 11, Title 11, United States Code|Chapter 11 bankruptcy]] for its recent roles in the [[List of California wildfires|California wildfires]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-pg-e-us-bankruptcy/pge-owner-of-biggest-u-s-power-utility-files-for-bankruptcy-idUSKCN1PN0PX (Reuters)] [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/pg-e-bankruptcy-californias-biggest-utility-wildfires-liability-camp-fire/ (CBS News)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[January 2019 North American cold wave]]
**Major midwestern cities, including [[Minneapolis]], [[Detroit]], [[Chicago]]  and [[Milwaukee]], are under severe wind chill advisories with wind chills approaching {{convert|−55|F|C}} at night. Michigan Governor [[Gretchen Whitmer]] and Wisconsin Governor [[Tony Evers]] declare states of emergency due to the record low windchill temperatures. [https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/local/breaking/ct-met-cold-weather-illinois-universities-closing-20190128-story.html (''Chicago Tribune'')] [https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/chicago-weather-what-is-closed-polar-vortex-2019-winter-windchill (''Chicago Sun-Times'')] [https://www.cbs58.com/news/major-winter-storm-today-then-frigid-rest-of-week (WDJT-TV)] [https://chicago.cbslocal.com/2019/01/29/chicago-deep-freeze-danger-extreme-cold-wind-chill-warning (WBBM-TV)] [https://www.wilx.com/content/news/Gov-Whitmer-declares-state-of-emergency-in-Michigan--505006832.html (WILX-TV)] [https://www.jsonline.com/story/weather/2019/01/28/wisconsin-snowstorm-milwaukee-wakes-up-blizzard-like-conditions/2698625002/ (''Milwaukee Journal Sentinel'')] 
*Two [[lions]], two [[hyenas]], a [[rhino]] and a [[giraffe]] are killed at [[Kruger National Park]], [[South Africa]], after storms topple a power cable. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-47047889 (BBC News)]
*[[Aviation accidents and incidents]]
** An air ambulance crashes in [[Ohio]], killing three crew members. The aircraft had been headed to [[Pomeroy, Ohio|Pomeroy]] to pick up a patient. [https://abc13.com/air-ambulance-helicopter-crash-kills-all-on-board/5111574/ (ABC News)]
** A second air ambulance, traveling from [[Anchorage, Alaska]] to the village of [[Kake, Alaska|Kake]], in [[Southeast Alaska]], was reported missing. The aircraft had a crew of three onboard. [https://www.ktuu.com/content/news/Guardian-Flight-aircraft-missing-in-SE-Alaska-505067391.html (KTUU)]

;Law and crime
*[[Asia Bibi blasphemy case]]
**Asia Bibi's blasphemy acquittal is upheld by [[Supreme Court of Pakistan|Pakistan's Supreme Court]]. She may seek asylum. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/jan/29/asia-bibi-pakistans-top-court-upholds-blasphemy-acquittal (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Foreign fighters in the Syrian and Iraqi Civil Wars]]
**About 130 [[French people|French citizens]] who joined the [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|Islamic State]] are expected to be returned to [[France]] by their Kurdish captors to face trial. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2019-01-29/france-will-take-back-130-isis-french-fighters-bfm-reports (Bloomberg)] [https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20190129-france-to-repatriate-130-daesh-fighters-for-trial/ (Middle East Monitor)]
*[[2010–2017 Toronto serial homicides|Toronto serial homicides]]
**Bruce McArthur, a Toronto landscaper charged on January 18, 2018, in this decade-long investigation, pleads guilty in [[Ontario Superior Court of Justice|Ontario Superior Court]] to murdering eight men. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-47047394 (BBC News)]
*[[Brumadinho dam disaster]]
**Police arrest five men, three from the mining company [[Vale (company)|Vale]] and two engineers from a subsidiary company, in connection with the mine collapse. [https://www.bbc.com/news/47044292 (BBC News)]
*[[Belgians|Belgian]] authorities order DNA tests of children recently adopted from the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] following reports that several parents thought they were sending their children to a [[Kinshasa]] holiday camp not an orphanage. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-47042241 (Reuters via BBC News)]
*Jussie Smollett reports being attacked by white racists in Chacago, IL 2:00 a.m. Report turned out not to be true. [https://abcnews.go.com/Entertainment/wireStory/timeline-events-jussie-smollett-reported-attack-81663217 (ABC News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[State of Palestine|Palestinian]] [[Prime Minister of the State of Palestine|Prime Minister]] [[Rami Hamdallah|Rami Al-Hamdallah]], along with  his unity government, resign from [[President of the State of Palestine|President]] [[Mahmoud Abbas]]'s government. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-palestinians-politics/palestinian-prime-minister-government-resign-idUSKCN1PN15Z (Reuters)]
*[[Brexit negotiations]]
**Votes in [[Parliament of the United Kingdom|parliament]] call for a no-deal outcome to be avoided, but do not support any delay in the [[Brexit]] timetable, and ask for the proposed customs arrangements in Ireland to be renegotiated, which the EU rejects. [https://edition.cnn.com/uk/live-news/brexit-deal-amendments-vote-gbr-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*[[2019 Venezuelan presidential crisis]]
**Following a request by Venezuelan Prosecutor General [[Tarek William Saab]], the [[Supreme Tribunal of Justice (Venezuela)|Supreme Tribunal of Justice]] bars the [[National Assembly of Venezuela|National Assembly]]-backed President [[Juan Guaidó]] from leaving the country and freezes his bank accounts and assets. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/the_americas/venezuelan-officials-seek-to-block-us-supported-opposition-leader-juan-guaido-from-leaving-the-country-freeze-his-assets/2019/01/29/1a4791a0-232c-11e9-b5b4-1d18dfb7b084_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]

;Science and technology
*A bug in [[Apple Inc]]'s [[FaceTime]] software is reported to have allowed users to spy on other devices. [https://edition.cnn.com/2019/01/28/tech/apple-face-time-bug/index.html (CNN)]
